pr_title: Add promtool command to check expressions
pr_body:
Adds command to check expressions

```
promtool check expressions --help
usage: promtool check expressions

Pass Prometheus expressions over stdin to check if they are valid.

Each line is considered a separate expression.

examples:

$ cat expressions.prom | promtool check expressions

Flags:
  -h, --help     Show context-sensitive help (also try --help-long and --help-man).
      --version  Show application version.
```
Closes https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/7167
pr_comments:
Thanks for the contribution!

I'm not sure about "each line is a separate expression". e.g. Grafana is mentioned in the issue; I happily use multiple lines in my Grafana queries (it's quite useful to put a comment above a query for example, or break up an expression). I also don't believe there's any other place in Prometheus where PromQL is treated as a single line, so this would be an anomaly.

(Closest I can think of is promtool query instant, as it's PromQL on a command line, but still, this works:
```shell
$ promtool query instant http://prometheus.demo.do.prometheus.io "# test query
up +
0"
{env="demo", instance="demo.do.prometheus.io:9093", job="alertmanager"} => 1 @[1624957836.518]
[snip]
```
)

I kind of think it would be better to first implement `promtool check expression`, that either takes an expression as a parameter (like `query instant` does), or if no parameter, reads stdin. That way if you want the behaviour of "each line is an expression", you can do something like `<expressions.prom xargs -n1 -d '\n' promtool check expression` without Prometheus having to compromise on what PromQL looks like.
@dgl I've used a double loop to parse the file now, so there's no requirement to have promQL queries be limited to a  single line. let me know what you think!

Thanks, for the update and sorry for the delay, took me a while to test this out.

I'm afraid this still has problems, for example:

```
$ ./promtool check expressions
up
*1
invalid 'expr': cannot be parsed: *1
$ ./promtool check expressions
# example
up
invalid 'expr': cannot be parsed: # example
```

We can't assume that if an expression parses without an error it is a complete expression.

I think like I said we should go for the minimal viable approach of implementing `check expression` rather than trying to make a way to check a list of expressions that takes those expressions in a new format not used elsewhere in Prometheus.

thanks for the review!
since we can't accept multiple promQL queries in the input file without creating new DSL to separate them from one another, i've reverted the commits that attempted to do so.

We discussed this during our bug scrub.

We believe that this functionality is essentially implemente by the `promtool promql format` command.

Therefore, we will close this. @dgl if you think there is something in this PR that is still worthy to resurrect, please follow up.

issue_context.title: promtool should support checking a single expression
issue_context.body:
Currently promtool support checking multiple expressions as defined in a rule file. If you want to lint a single expression, you need to arbitrarily/needlessly stick the expression in a rule file. 

I propose extending promtool with the sub-command `promtool check expressions` that takes a number of expressions from a file or stdin, with one expression per line to be checked. Notably, this proposal does not support multi-line rules. After all, we're not in the context of YAML.

This functionality is especially useful when preparing promql expressions for other systems like Grafana. In my case, I'm managing Grafana dashboards in Git so I don't have the Grafana GUI to quickly tell me that my promql is invalid. I'd like to lint my Grafana JSON, extract the promql, and run it through a checker.
comments: Maybe, a flag like `-i` for instantaneous checking of expressions might be better after `promtool check expressions` for implementing this.
If we need this feature to be implemented, I would like to pick this up.
Looking forward to use this feature 🙂

Following the lead of `check metrics`, I think it makes sense to pass in any file contents over stdin:

```
cat expressions.txt | promtool check expressions
```

For single expressions (besides just `echo "expr" | ...`) we could support:

```
promtool check expression expr
```

But I'm not sure if it's necessary
Hello from the bug scrub, this has been implemented via the [promtool promql format](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/command-line/promtool/#promtool-promql-format) command line tool.

review_comments: can we add `in = ""` as a test case?
same here, can we update this usage string to indicate only 1 expression is accepted at a time

s/expressions/expression/g
since we are only passing in 1 expression at a time, does `exprs` need to be a list?

line 621 and 622 show up on the same line, can we add a space between those 2 lines so they are separate?
```
$ ./promtool check expressions --help
usage: promtool check expressions [<expression>]

Pass Prometheus expressions over stdin or as an optional argument to check if they are valid. If passed over stdin, command assumes each line is a single expression.

examples:

$ promtool check expressions "rate(my_counter[5m])" $ cat expressions.prom | promtool check expressions

Flags:
  -h, --help                 Show context-sensitive help (also try --help-long and --help-man).
      --version              Show application version.
      --enable-feature= ...  Comma separated feature names to enable (only PromQL related). See https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/feature_flags/ for the options and more details.

Args:
  [<expression>]  The expression to check.
```
